title: Identification of Untreated Cohort Means in Short Panels with Missing Outcomes via Rank-Two Certificates

gap_reasons: It does not deliver the advertised identification iff: certificate failure is explicitly shown not to imply causal-target nonidentification under the stated class.

Likewise, the results named a singular or minimax frontier have no positive risk converse, honest-width converse, or necessary consistency threshold; the proved rate statements are achievable upper guarantees only.

Because the combinatorial certificate is published background and the new causal transport is a direct covariance-eigenspace reconstruction under spherical errors, the remaining contribution is useful but too narrow and incomplete for the field floor.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery verified the published generic rank-two projection certificate, derived the observed-law reconstruction and strict O3-containment witness, and established radius-adaptive PCA risk and honest-rectangle upper guarantees. The intended converse and matching lower frontiers collapsed because an allowed tight-radius family has an identically zero causal target even when the certificate fails and singular shells are nonempty. A future specification would need independently motivated quantitative nondegeneracy, rather than adding it here to assume the missing deformation.
tldr: Short panels with systematic missing outcomes require gluing cohort-specific covariance eigenspaces before missing untreated means become causal functionals. A deterministic smallest-two anchor convention maps every mask to the published rank-two count certificate of Pimentel--Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak, with Streinu--Theran pebble recognition and extraction as background. When the certificate passes, the observed local eigenspaces determine the global factor plane and an explicit complete-observed-law map recovers every untreated cohort-time mean. When it fails, the factor plane is generically nonunique, but the frozen primitive class does not imply causal-target nonidentification because an allowed tight-radius class has \(\mu=0\) throughout. The panel-specific corollary \(O_3\Rightarrow\) certificate acceptance is strict for masks \(123,145,256,346\). Covariance PCA gives the unconditional squared-risk upper bound \(\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2,C_0/(Ns_N^2)\}\), and robust profile-recentered moment inversion gives uniformly honest rectangles with upper half-width \(\min\{b_\lambda,C_\alpha\min(1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1})\}\). The universal same-shell deformation questions have negative answers on the zero-target boundary. Construction of a frontier-scale testing pair on a quantitatively nondegenerate frozen-model subclass, and a corresponding honest-width lower bound, remain open; \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient but not necessary for consistency. The frozen stochastic class is not the full Lei--Ross class and does not itself assume strict exogeneity; its overlap with Lei--Ross is the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error subclass.
gap: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak already provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion, and Streinu and Theran provide sparse-hypergraph pebble machinery. Lei and Ross provide \(O_3\)-sufficient identification and regular APM inference. What is absent is the causal transport from the published certificate to equality of complete observed panel laws, plus a mathematically total finite-moment inversion rule and a legal same-shell lower experiment for missing cohort means.
fill: The paper takes the published count and pebble results as inputs, proves their distinct full-law causal transport and countermodel consequence, and records \(O_3\) containment with the exact four-mask strict witness. It develops covariance-PCA risk bounds and profile-recentered inversion of a robust data-driven \(\ell_\infty\) joint-moment ball. Two-sided statistical frontiers are stated only conditional on legal same-shell deformations, with the four-mask path isolated as the early-kill obligation.
